title: Swing-fraction serial memory does not improve cross-dataset Parkinson probability prediction in a small-source transfer test
abstract: Swing and stance subphase dynamics may contain information absent from stride variability. We tested one short-lag swing-fraction memory scalar against demographic, stride and swing summary measures, using31 gaitndd participants for training and153 gaitpdb participants for frozen testing. Adding lag-one swing-fraction correlation changed external Brier from 0.324931 to 0.327361 (delta +0.002431; joint source/target bootstrap95% interval [-0.026992,+0.025016]); the prespecified incremental-benefit criterion was not met. AUC increased from 0.623879 to 0.673741, but probability accuracy worsened and both models underperformed a source-prevalence constant. This exploratory negative result is conditional on the estimator, case mix and small training sample; it neither establishes equivalence nor excludes physiological information in subphase dynamics. A raw-data audit found officially byte-identical JuCo26/JuPt01 recordings under opposite labels. Excluding both left151 target records and Brier delta +0.002619 (joint95% interval [-0.030602,+0.028170]), supporting the same narrow negative conclusion.
